sample_unit: radiology reports (evaluated by 4 neuroradiologists and 4 patient volunteers)

links.outcome: Patient confidence, satisfaction with jargon and time to understand: original report vs ChatGPT plain-language summary
links.effect: Confidence in understanding 98% (116/118) with summary vs 26% (31/118) with report; jargon satisfaction 91% vs 8%; time to understand 97% vs 23%.
links.quote: After reading the summary, patient confidence in understanding (98%, 116/118 vs 26%, 31/118) and satisfaction regarding the level of jargon/terminology (91%, 107/118 vs 8%, 9/118) and time taken to understand the content (97%, 115/118 vs 23%, 27/118) substantially improved.

links.outcome: Radiologist-rated omissions and over/underemphasis errors in AI-generated report summaries
links.effect: Missing relevant information in 5% (6/120) of responses; overemphasis of nonsignificant findings 12% (14/120); underemphasis of significant findings 18% (22/120); no fabricated findings.
links.quote: Five percent (6/120) of responses indicated there was missing relevant medical information in the summary, 12% (14/120) reported instances of overemphasis of nonsignificant findings, and 18% (22/120) reported instances of underemphasis of significant findings.

screen.reason: The study evaluates the accuracy, readability, and patient understandability of ChatGPT-generated patient-friendly radiology report summaries compared to original reports, but does not test a specific deployment practice or guardrail intervention.
